title: AQ Podcast | Brazil's Scandal-Plagued Election
gist: Brazil's October 2026 presidential race has swung from Lula as clear favorite to a polling tie with Flávio Bolsonaro gaining momentum, driven not by the economy or security but by the Daniel Vorcaro banking scandal, whose alleged ties shifted from Bolsonaro to Justice Alexandre de Moraes. AQ's podcast with Thomas Traumann also covers the economy and possible Trump intervention.

insights.claim: A few weeks ago there was near consensus that Lula was favored in Brazil's October 2026 election, but most polls now show a tie with Flávio Bolsonaro appearing to have momentum.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Rising odds of an opposition win may move Brazilian assets; election risk premium is now two-sided.
insights.quote: Today, most polls show the race is tied, and Flávio Bolsonaro seems to have the momentum.

themes.theme: Vorcaro scandal as the decisive issue

insights.claim: Unlike other recent Latin American elections, Brazil's campaign has been dominated not by the economy or security but by a corruption scandal around disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro, whose network extended across the political and economic establishment.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Scandal news flow, not macro data, is driving Brazil election odds; monitor Vorcaro revelations.
insights.locator: In recent months, the main issue

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro was badly damaged in May by alleged ties to Vorcaro, but attention has since shifted to Vorcaro's alleged ties to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, which appear to have damaged Lula; all deny wrongdoing.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Scandal momentum can flip quickly; avoid high-conviction election positioning.
insights.locator: Back in May, Bolsonaro was badly damaged

insights.claim: A key open question in Brazil's race is whether President Trump will try to intervene on behalf of the Bolsonaro family.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Possible US intervention (tariffs, designations) is a wildcard for Brazil risk around the vote.
